pathogens.name: Avian Influenza (Highly Pathogenic / Low Pathogenic)
pathogens.transmission: Direct bird-to-bird contact, migratory waterfowl, contaminated water, fomites.
clinicalSigns: Facial cyanosis/swelling of comb and wattles
biosecurityMeasures: Strict restriction of farm visitors and equipment
Mandatory notification to Upazila Livestock Officer (ULO)
pathogens.amrRelevance: Viral disease. Antibiotics have zero therapeutic effect and must never be administered.

pathogens.name: Newcastle Disease (Ranikhet)
clinicalSigns: Nervous signs (torticollis / twisted neck, circling, tremors)
biosecurityMeasures: Strict adherence to BCRDV / RDV vaccination schedules
Proper bird disposal (deep burial with lime or incineration)
pathogens.amrRelevance: Viral etiology. Antibiotic administration is completely ineffective and violates AMR guidelines.

pathogens.name: Infectious Bursal Disease (Gumboro)
pathogens.transmission: Fecal-oral route; highly resistant in environment.
biosecurityMeasures: Thorough shed cleaning with formaldehyde or virucidal disinfectant between batches
Breeder flock vaccination for maternal antibodies
pathogens.amrRelevance: Immunosuppressive viral disease. Supportive hydration (electrolytes) indicated; no antibiotics.

pathogens.name: Coccidiosis (Eimeria tenella, necatrix, acervulina)
pathogens.transmission: Ingestion of sporulated oocysts from wet, warm litter.
pathogens.amrRelevance: Protozoal infection. Antibacterials are ineffective. Requires antiprotozoals (e.g. toltrazuril/amprolium) under veterinary instruction.

pathogens.name: Infectious Coryza (Avibacterium paragallinarum)
pathogens.transmission: Direct contact, airborne droplets, contaminated drinking water.
pathogens.amrRelevance: Requires bacterial culture and Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing (AST) before therapeutic intervention.
